land.text: the County of Castile as Cliopatria draws it from 961

predecessors.note: 'In 931 the county was reunified by Count Fernán González, who rose in rebellion against the Kingdom of León' (County of Castile page); the Leon page: 'The County of Castile split off in 931'. The county 'traces its origins to the 9th-century County of Castile, as an eastern frontier lordship of the Kingdom of León'. Cliopatria's Castile row begins in 961 and keeps the county inside León's shape to 960.

land.text: Castile and León, united for good in 1230

successors.note: 'The Kingdoms of Castile and of León, with their southern acquisitions, came to be known collectively as the Crown of Castile.' Cliopatria's Crown of Castile row begins in 1236 (311,118 km2), after Córdoba fell in 1236 (Ferdinand III page); the Castile row ends in 1235 although the pages unite the crowns in 1230.

capitals.name: Burgos
capitals.note: The pages give no capital: 'Capital: No settled capital' (Kingdom of Castile infobox), 'Castile didn't have a permanent capital' (County of Castile page, a footnote naming Burgos, Valladolid and Toledo as centres of royal authority). Burgos is the county's centre and stands for the whole life; Toledo (taken 25 May 1085) was the court of Alfonso VI, who 'died in Toledo on 1 July 1109'.

correction.text: the County of Castile as Cliopatria draws it from 961

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 931-960: Cliopatria's Castile row begins in 961 while the pages date the county's reunification and its break with León to 931 ('In 931 the county was reunified by Count Fernán González, who rose in rebellion against the Kingdom of León'; the Leon page: 'The County of Castile split off in 931'). The county is taken to have the outline Cliopatria draws from 961; neither page gives a boundary. The Ramiro II page (Leon dossier) has Fernán González win 'brief de facto independence' only late in Ramiro's reign (to 951), so 931-950 is a county in rebellion rather than a recognised state.

39,927 km2 for 961-1009: Burgos (52 of 56 cells), Soria, La Rioja, Cantabria and a strip of Segovia: 'the northern reaches of the Sistema Central, just north of modern-day Madrid province'. 'achieved an autonomous status, allowing the county to be inherited by his family'. Neither Castile page gives an infobox area, so no ratio.
39,998 km2 for 1010-1027: the same county, held by the counts down to García Sánchez, 'assassinated in 1028 while in León to marry the princess Sancha'.

correction.text: the county under Sancho III's overlordship, then Ferdinand's

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1028-1039: Cliopatria has no Castile shape for 1028-1039. After the assassination of Count García Sánchez in 1028 'Sancho III, acting as feudal overlord, appointed his younger son' Ferdinand, 'count of Castile from his uncle's death in 1029' (Ferdinand I page); 'Following Sancho's death in 1035, Castile returned to the nominal control of León'. The county keeps its outline; the kingdom-of-pamplona dossier (eu-12-a) draws it inside Navarre 1028-1035, which this dossier records as a loss and a gain.

34,277 km2 for 1040-1045: the county without most of La Rioja (5 of 21 cells against 20 in 1010). Ferdinand I, count since 1029, is king in León from 1038 but Castile is still its own realm ('Independent kingdom (1065–1230)' in the infobox is later). The La Rioja loss is not on a page opened (unverified: page budget).

correction.text: Ferdinand I's realm with Lamego (1057), Viseu (1058) and Coimbra (1064) added

keyframe_review.note: 167,203 km2 for 1046-1065: Ferdinand I's two crowns drawn as one Castile shape (León, Galicia and the Duero; 626 cells). The shape lacks his Mondego conquests, which the page dates: 'On 29 November 1057 his army conquered Lamego and its valleys', 'first taking Viseu ... on 25 July 1058', Coimbra 'taken on 25 July 1064 after a six-month siege'. Corrected from those years. Cliopatria's Castile 1072 shape (the earliest to hold the Mondego) shows them.

43,201 km2 for 1066-1071: Sancho II's Castile after 'By his will, Ferdinand divided his kingdom among his three sons' (the infobox of the Kingdom of Castile page: '1065–1072: Sancho II'). The shape reaches Madrid and Guadalajara in the south.

correction.text: the 1072 shape with La Rioja and the Basque lands added from 1076

keyframe_review.note: 201,772 km2 for 1072-1084: the reunited realm of Alfonso VI ('and Castile (1072–1109)'), with Galicia and León. The shape lacks the Basque lands and La Rioja, which Cliopatria adds only in 1085: 'Alfonso VI annexed the territories of Álava, Vizcaya, part of Guipúzcoa and La Bureba' and, from the Navarre page, took La Rioja after 4 June 1076. The shape holds from 1072, with these lands added from 1076.
245,563 km2 for 1085-1093: Toledo, Cuenca and Guadalajara added: 'Toledo, which finally fell on 25 May 1085'. 'In the Council of Burgos in 1080' is the Kingdom of Castile page's court.

245,272 km2 for 1094-1098: the 1085 shape. Lisbon, Sintra and Santarém, obtained as the price of an alliance, were lost in November 1094 and Badajoz fell to the Almoravids; the shape keeps the Portuguese lands from Minho to Santarém that the page calls the County of Portugal 'from the Minho river to Santarém'. Unverified: page budget.

correction.text: the 1099 shape without Valencia and Castellón, from 1102

keyframe_review.note: 257,218 km2 for 1099-1110: Valencia (30 of 42 cells) and Castellón are added. 'his widow, Jimena, was governing the city' in 1099 and 'Alfonso VI supervised the evacuation of Valencia in March and April' of 1102, after which the Almoravids took the ruins. The shape holds 1099-1101; from 1102 Valencia and Castellón are out.

155,401 km2 for 1111-1125: Urraca's realm, without Galicia ('crowned and anointed Alfonso King of Galicia in the cathedral of Santiago de Compostela' in 1111) and without Portugal. The Alfonso VII page does not describe Urraca's reign or the wars with Alfonso I of Aragon ('before he repudiated her in 1114' is the Castile page's line); the shape stands, unverified: page budget.

correction.text: Castile proper: the 1139 shape without the León shape of 1126

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1126-1138: Cliopatria's León row holds Alfonso VII's realm in these years (192,464 km2) and draws no Castile. Castile proper is taken as the 1139 shape minus the León shape of 1126 (Burgos, Soria, Cantabria, La Rioja, the Basque lands, Segovia: 161 cells). 'On 10 March 1126 ... he was crowned in León' and 'By the Peace of Támara of 1127, the Battler recognised Alfonso VII of Castile'.

187,517 km2 for 1139-1146: Alfonso VII's whole realm drawn as Castile, without the Portuguese lands (the County of Portugal row 1139-1146; 'recognized as independent de jure in 1143'). 'On 26 May 1135, Alfonso was crowned "Emperor of Spain" in the Cathedral of León.'

correction.text: the 1152 shape, with Almería, applied from October 1147

keyframe_review.note: 216,087 km2 for 1147-1151: Calatrava and the Tagus country (Ciudad Real 69 of 77 cells), Toledo and Coria (Cáceres 37). 'In 1142, Alfonso besieged Coria a second time and took it'; 'which was occupied in October 1147' (Almería); 'In 1144, he advanced as far as Córdoba'. Almería is in Cliopatria's 1152 shape only, so the 1152 shape is applied from October 1147. The Calatrava step is not on the page (unverified: page budget).

216,906 km2 for 1152-1168: still the whole of Alfonso VII's realm, although he died on 21 August 1157 'by dividing his realm between his sons' (Sancho III got Castile). The shape holds for 1152-1156, with Almería, which 'entered into Almohad possession' (1157); from 1157 the realm is split (castile_1157).

correction.text: Castile under Sancho III and Alfonso VIII, apart from León

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1157-1168: Castile alone, as Cliopatria draws it from 1169 (106,420 km2). 'Between 1072 and 1157, it was again united with León, and after 1230, the union became permanent.'

106,420 km2 for 1169-1187: Castile without León, Toledo to the Guadiana (Ciudad Real 68 of 77 cells). 'In 1174, he ceded Uclés to the Order of Santiago' (Alfonso VIII page): the military orders' lands are not drawn separately in Cliopatria. Cuenca fell in 1177 ('the Conquest of Cuenca in 1177'; surrendered 21 September), already inside the shape (Cuenca 36 of 68 cells).

union.text: the part of La Rioja that the 1202 shape holds and the 1188 shape does not

correction.text: the 1188 shape with the La Rioja of 1202

keyframe_review.note: 106,179 km2 for 1188-1201: the 1169 shape. 'In 1186, he recovered part of La Rioja from the Kingdom of Navarre' (the shape holds 5 of 21 La Rioja cells; the 1202 shape holds 20). Holds 1188-1194; part of La Rioja added.

union.text: the part of La Rioja that the 1202 shape holds and the 1188 shape does not

correction.text: Castile without the Calatrava country after Alarcos

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1195-1199: 'he was roundly defeated by the caliph Abu Yusuf Yaqub al-Mansur. The Almohads then retook territory, starting with Calatrava.' Calatrava lies in Ciudad Real (68 of 77 cells are inside the 1188 shape). The page gives no list of lost lands, so the whole province is taken out as the reading; 'In 1195, the Almohads defeated Alfonso VIII of Castile in the Battle of Alarcos' (Las Navas de Tolosa page).

correction.text: the 1202 shape without the Calatrava country, 1200-1211

keyframe_review.note: 116,987 km2 for 1202-1215: La Rioja (20 of 21 cells), Álava, Vizcaya and Guipúzcoa are added. 'By 1200 the conquest of western Navarre was complete' (Navarre page), two years before the shape; the Calatrava country is still out until Las Navas. The shape holds 1200-1211 without Ciudad Real.

correction.text: the 1202 shape with Baeza and Úbeda and the Calatrava country back

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1212-1215: 'took place on 16 July 1212'; 'Shortly after the battle, the Castilians took Baeza' and 'then conquered Úbeda'. The Calatrava country returns to Castile with the campaign (bridge: the page does not say; conf 1 in the ledger).

156,417 km2 for 1216-1226: Albacete, southern Cuenca, northern Jaén (32 of 54 cells) and Córdoba (16 of 51). Only Baeza and Úbeda are dated (1212, Las Navas page); 'In 1225, a Castilian army accompanied al-Bayyasi in a campaign' and 'the Castilians remained in occupation of al-Bayyasi's holdings in Andújar, Baeza and Martos' (Ferdinand III page). Most of the +39,400 km2 over 1202 is unverified: page budget.
156,343 km2 for 1227-1235: the same shape; years 1227-1230 as Castile alone (castile_1231 follows). 'In 1228, a new Almohad pretender, Idris al-Ma'mun, decided to abandon Spain.'

union.text: all of León as it stood in 1230

correction.text: Castile and León, one realm from the treaty of Benavente

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1231-1235: 'The resulting treaty of Benavente was signed on 11 December 1230' and 'When Ferdinand's father died in 1230, his will delivered the kingdom to his older daughters': Ferdinand III holds Castile and León. Cliopatria draws both shapes to 1235; the Leon dossier ends at the union, so this shape is the union.

region.text: the County of Castile as Cliopatria draws it from 961

ledger.note: 931: Fernán González reunifies the county of Castile. 'In 931 the county was reunified by Count Fernán González, who rose in rebellion against the Kingdom of León' (the Kingdom of Castile page repeats the sentence; the Leon page: 'The County of Castile split off in 931'). The pages give no boundary, so the region is Cliopatria's county shape from 961.

region.text: the County of Castile under Sancho III's overlordship

ledger.note: 1028: Sancho III of Navarre takes the county's government. 'García was assassinated in 1028 while in León to marry the princess Sancha'; 'Sancho III, acting as feudal overlord, appointed his younger son' (County of Castile page, undated); Ferdinand was 'count of Castile from his uncle's death in 1029'. The kingdom-of-pamplona dossier has the same step as a gain in 1028.

1035: Ferdinand takes Castile on his father's death. 'After his father's death on 18 October 1035, Ferdinand continued to rule in Castile'; 'Following Sancho's death in 1035, Castile returned to the nominal control of León' (Kingdom of Castile page).

region.text: León, drawn inside the Castile row 1046-1065

ledger.note: 1046: Ferdinand I's realm is drawn as one Castile shape. Cliopatria's Castile row jumps from 34,277 km2 (1045) to 167,203 km2 (1046), taking in León and Galicia, which it had drawn apart in 1040-1045. The pages date only Tamarón (4 September 1037: 'defeated and killed his suzerain') and the coronation in León (22 June 1038); the 1046 date is Cliopatria's.

region.text: La Bureba and the Tirón valley

ledger.note: 1054: Atapuerca. 'On 15 September 1054, Ferdinand defeated his elder brother García at the' battle of Atapuerca (the Pamplona dossier has García killed and Ferdinand taking La Bureba and the Tirón valley). The page names no land; the region is La Bureba read from the Pamplona dossier.
1057: Lamego falls. 'On 29 November 1057 his army conquered Lamego and its valleys.' The page names no holder; the taifa-of-badajoz dossier (eu-12-a) is the neighbour on this side.
1058: Viseu falls. 'first taking Viseu in its middle stretch on 25 July 1058'.

1060: Zaragoza pays Ferdinand parias. 'In 1060, according to the Historia silense, Ferdinand invaded the taifa of Zaragoza'; the emir 'submitted to Ferdinand and agreed to pay parias'. A tributary, drawn as a lighter tint.

1062: Toledo pays Ferdinand parias. 'In 1062, Ferdinand invaded the east of al-Mamun's taifa'; 'After seeing his country plundered, al-Mamun agreed to pay parias and Ferdinand left.' Alfonso VI took refuge with 'his vassal Al-Mamun' in 1072 (Alfonso VI page).
1064: Coimbra falls. 'was taken on 25 July 1064 after a six-month siege' (the Badajoz dossier's page has the city entered on 9 July 1064 and delivered to Sesnando Davides).

1065: the county becomes a kingdom. 'Independent kingdom (1065–1230)'; infobox 'Established: 1065'; 'it was not until 1065 that it was separated from the Kingdom of León' (County of Castile page); '1065–1072: Sancho II (first)'. Same state, same colour (rule 2).
1065: Ferdinand's realm is divided; León goes to Alfonso. 'By his will, Ferdinand divided his kingdom among his three sons'; 'Ferdinand died on 24 December 1065, in León'. Sancho keeps Castile.
1065: Galicia is carved off. 'the region of Galicia was carved off to create a separate state' for García.
1071: Sancho II invades Galicia. 'Sancho invaded Galicia in 1071, defeating their brother García II who was arrested in Santarém.' Alfonso 'had tacitly supported the invasion'.

1072: Sancho II defeats Alfonso at Golpejera and takes León. 'The truce was broken with the Battle of Golpejera on 12 January 1072.' Sancho is murdered in the siege of Zamora in the same year and Alfonso VI 'reclaim[s] his throne as well as Sancho's and Garcia's original inheritances': Castile, León and Galicia, one realm to 1109.
1074: Granada pays Alfonso VI. Alfonso 'probably recovered payment of the parias of Toledo' and Granada's taifa 'consequently also began to pay him taxes'.

1076: the Basque lands are annexed. 'Alfonso VI annexed the territories of Álava, Vizcaya, part of Guipúzcoa and La Bureba' (the page ties them to the Navarrese succession crisis of 1076). Cliopatria shows them from 1085.

Zaragoza's earlier parias to Ferdinand (1060) lapse before 1076: the page's wording 'resume payment' implies a gap, but it dates neither the stop nor the cause. Placed at the resumption so the two relations do not overlap.
1076: the emir of Zaragoza resumes parias. 'The Emir of Zaragoza agreed to resume payment of the parias.' Zaragoza pays Alfonso VI again.

1076: Alfonso VI takes La Rioja. 'On 4 June 1076, a conspiracy involving Sancho IV's brother Ramón and sister Ermesinda ended with the murder of the king'; 'Alfonso VI of León and Castile took control of La Rioja' while Sancho Ramírez of Aragon took the rest.
1079: Coria is conquered. 'In 1079, he conquered Coria.' The page names no holder; Coria belonged to the neighbouring taifa of Badajoz.
1085: Alfonso VI takes Toledo. 'Toledo, which finally fell on 25 May 1085.' The Kingdom of Castile page credits 'the kingdom of Castile's conquest of the great cultural center of Toledo (1085)'.
1085: Toledo, a tributary since 1062, is annexed on 25 May 1085.

1086: the taifas stop paying after Sagrajas. 'The Leonese and Castilian armies suffered decisive defeats in the battles of Sagrajas (1086)' and 'As a consequence of the serious defeat, the Andalusian taifas stopped paying the parias.' The page dates neither stop; Granada and Zaragoza are placed at the battle.
1086: Zaragoza's parias stop after Sagrajas (see the Granada line); Zaragoza is again 'his vassal Al-Mustain II' in 1097.

1094: Lisbon, Sintra and Santarém are lost. 'As the price for this alliance, Alfonso VI had obtained Lisbon, Sintra, and Santarem, but lost them in November 1094.' (The Almoravid dossier names kingdom-of-leon as the loser.) Badajoz fell to the Almoravids the same year.
1097: Alfonso VI goes to Zaragoza 'to assist his vassal Al-Mustain II'.

1099: Valencia is governed for Alfonso VI. After El Cid's death 'his widow, Jimena, was governing the city'; El Cid had come 'to Toledo in late 1086 or early 1087' to reconcile with Alfonso and 'the recovery of Valencia in June' 1094 was his. The page does not call Valencia Alfonso's land before 1102; the date is Cliopatria's.

1102: Valencia is evacuated. 'Alfonso VI supervised the evacuation of Valencia in March and April' and burned the city; the Almoravids took the ruins in May. 'In 1102, Alfonso VI sent troops to help Valencia against the Almoravid threat.'

1110: the Almoravids take Zaragoza. The Taifa page (read for the Caliphate dossier) has 'Zaragoza ... 1046-1110 (to Almoravids)'; the pages opened for this dossier give no Zaragoza date after 1097, so 1110 is Cliopatria's last Zaragoza year.

1111: Alfonso Raimúndez is crowned king of Galicia. 'crowned and anointed Alfonso King of Galicia in the cathedral of Santiago de Compostela' (1111). Cliopatria draws a Galicia row 1111-1125 and a Castile shape without it.

region.text: the County of Portugal, from the Minho to Santarém

ledger.note: 1111: the Portuguese lands leave the shape. 'he gave Henry and Teresa the government of the County of Portugal' (Alfonso VI page; 'Some scholars argue this could not have happened before 1103'); the county comprised 'the lands from the Minho river to Santarém'. Cliopatria drops them from the Castile shape in 1111; the county-of-portugal dossier dates its founding to 1096.

region.text: the realm Cliopatria draws as León 1126-1138

ledger.note: 1126: Alfonso VII is crowned in León. 'On 10 March 1126, after the death of his mother, he was crowned in León.' Cliopatria draws his realm as the León row 1126-1138; Castile proper is drawn in the dossier's castile_1126 keyframe.

region.text: León, back inside the Castile row 1139-1168

ledger.note: 1139: Alfonso VII's whole realm is drawn as Castile again. 'The Peace of Támara of 1127' and 'Emperor of Spain' (26 May 1135) are on the page; nothing in 1139. Cliopatria's Castile row jumps to 187,517 km2 in 1139, when the County of Portugal row begins.
1142: Coria is retaken. 'In 1142, Alfonso besieged Coria a second time and took it.'

ledger.counterpart: Almería's Muslim holders (the page names none)
ledger.note: 1147: Almería is occupied. Almería 'was occupied in October 1147' by the Christian fleet and army; 'In 1144, he advanced as far as Córdoba'.
1157: Almería passes to the Almohads. 'Six years later, Almería entered into Almohad possession' (after the 1151 Treaty of Tudilén).

region.text: León, Galicia and the Extremaduran strip

ledger.note: 1157: León is split from Castile. 'Between 1072 and 1157, it was again united with León'; Alfonso VII died on 21 August 1157 and left Castile to Sancho III and León to Ferdinand II.

region.text: the part of La Rioja that the 1202 shape holds and the 1188 shape does not

ledger.note: 1186: part of La Rioja is recovered. 'In 1186, he recovered part of La Rioja from the Kingdom of Navarre.' Cliopatria shows La Rioja filled in only in 1202.

1195: Alarcos. 'he was roundly defeated by the caliph Abu Yusuf Yaqub al-Mansur. The Almohads then retook territory, starting with Calatrava.' The year is the Las Navas page's: 'In 1195, the Almohads defeated Alfonso VIII of Castile in the Battle of Alarcos'. The page lists no other lands; the province of Ciudad Real is the reading.

1200: western Navarre is conquered. 'By 1200 the conquest of western Navarre was complete.' The page names no provinces here; Álava and Guipúzcoa are the reading (they are in Cliopatria's 1202 shape).

region.text: the Calatrava country returns to Castile

ledger.note: 1212: the Calatrava country returns to Castile. Bridge: the page does not say; the campaign marched through it and the Cliopatria shapes put Ciudad Real back in Castile by 1216.
1212: Baeza and Úbeda after Las Navas de Tolosa. 'took place on 16 July 1212'; 'Shortly after the battle, the Castilians took Baeza' and then conquered Úbeda.
1225: Andújar, Baeza and Martos. 'In 1225, a Castilian army accompanied al-Bayyasi in a campaign'; 'the Castilians remained in occupation of al-Bayyasi's holdings in Andújar, Baeza and Martos'.

region.text: all of León as it stood in 1230

ledger.note: 1230: Castile and León are united for good. 'The resulting treaty of Benavente was signed on 11 December 1230'; 'When Ferdinand's father died in 1230, his will delivered the kingdom to his older daughters'. The Kingdom of Castile infobox gives 'Permanent union of Castile and León: 23 September 1230' (the Leon dossier's page: 10 December).

union.text: all of León as it stood in 1230

region.text: Castile and León, the realm of Ferdinand III

ledger.note: 1235: the Castile row ends; the Crown of Castile row begins in 1236 (Cliopatria). The pages put the permanent union in 1230 and Córdoba's conquest in 1236 ('the old Umayyad capital of Córdoba in 1236', Ferdinand III page); the state does not end in 1235, it is called the Crown of Castile ('collectively as the Crown of Castile', Kingdom of Castile page).

wars.name: Battle of Tamarón and Ferdinand I's conquest of León
wars.outcome: Ferdinand I, count of Castile, 'defeated and killed his suzerain at the Battle of Tamarón on 4 September 1037' and was crowned king in León on 22 June 1038: two kingdoms, one king.
wars.note: No border moves: Cliopatria draws León separately 1040-1045 and inside the Castile row 1046-1065.

wars.name: Battle of Atapuerca

zones.text: La Bureba and the Tirón valley

wars.outcome: 'On 15 September 1054, Ferdinand defeated his elder brother García' at Atapuerca; García of Navarre was killed.

wars.name: Ferdinand I's Mondego conquests and parias campaigns
wars.outcome: Lamego (29 November 1057), Viseu (25 July 1058) and Coimbra (25 July 1064) conquered; Zaragoza (1060) and Toledo (1062) agreed to pay parias; 'Seville, and probably Badajoz also, paid a ransom for his withdrawal' (1063); 1065 was 'his last military campaign' (Valencia).

wars.name: War of the sons of Ferdinand I
wars.outcome: Sancho II took Galicia (1071) and León (Golpejera, 12 January 1072) and was murdered at Zamora; Alfonso VI took back León, and took Castile and Galicia.
wars.note: 'The conflicts began after the death of their mother Queen Sancha on 7 November 1067.'

wars.name: Conquest of Toledo and the Almoravid wars of Alfonso VI
wars.outcome: Toledo fell 25 May 1085; defeats at Sagrajas (1086) and Uclés (29 May 1108, where his only son Sancho was killed); Almoravid attacks in June 1090 and 1097; Lisbon, Sintra and Santarém lost in November 1094; Valencia evacuated in spring 1102; Alfonso VI died 1 July 1109.

wars.name: Reign of Urraca and wars with Alfonso I of Aragon
wars.outcome: Not read: the Alfonso VII page does not describe Urraca's reign; it gives Alfonso Raimúndez crowned king of Galicia in 1111 and 'By the Peace of Támara of 1127, the Battler recognised Alfonso VII'.
wars.note: Gap for a reviewer: open Urraca of León and Castile.

wars.name: Alfonso VII's campaigns against the Almoravids and the Almohad invasion
wars.outcome: Coria retaken 1142; Córdoba reached 1144; Almería occupied October 1147 and lost to the Almohads by 1157; 'Two years later, the Almohads invaded'; Portugal independent de jure by the Treaty of Zamora (1143); the Treaty of Tudilén (1151) with Ramon Berenguer.

wars.name: Castilian conquest of western Navarre
wars.outcome: '(1173–1176)' invasion of Navarre, Henry II of England arbitrated in 1177, La Rioja and the Bureba lost for good by Navarre, and 'By 1200 the conquest of western Navarre was complete.'

wars.name: Alarcos and the Almohad war
wars.outcome: Alfonso VIII 'roundly defeated' at Alarcos in 1195; the Almohads retook Calatrava and in 1196-1197 'attacked several important Castilian cities including Toledo' (the Las Navas page does not say they fell).

wars.name: Battle of Las Navas de Tolosa
wars.outcome: 16 July 1212: Alfonso VIII, Peter II of Aragon and Sancho VII of Navarre (with a Portuguese contingent) defeat the Almohad caliph al-Nasir; Baeza and Úbeda taken shortly after. 'Alfonso IX of León stood aloof'.

wars.name: Ferdinand III's Andalusian campaigns to 1235
wars.outcome: Castile occupies al-Bayyasi's Andújar, Baeza and Martos after 1225; the Almohad pretender Idris al-Ma'mun abandoned Spain in 1228; Córdoba falls in 1236 (outside this dossier).

certainty.note: Every frontier is a march of castles and raids; the pages opened give no surveyed line. The Treaty of Cazola (1179) 'defined' the zones of expansion of Castile and Aragon (Alfonso VIII page) and the Treaty of Almizra (1244) is outside the life; neither is a boundary survey. The Castile-León line is soft throughout.

sources.title: Kingdom of Castile
sources.note: Identity: established 1065, no settled capital, 931 reunification, the 1072-1157 and 1230 unions, rulers 1065-1072 (Sancho II) to 1217-1230 (Ferdinand III); no infobox area.

sources.title: County of Castile
sources.note: The county: frontier lordship of León, Fernán González 931, autonomy, García Sánchez assassinated 1028, Sancho III's overlordship, 1065 separation, 'no permanent capital'.

sources.title: Ferdinand I of León
sources.note: Count of Castile 1029, Tamarón 1037, crowned in León 1038, Atapuerca 1054, Lamego 1057, Viseu 1058, Coimbra 1064, parias from Zaragoza 1060 and Toledo 1062, the division of 1065.

sources.title: Alfonso VI of León and Castile

notes: Cliopatria rows and what is not settled. (1) Start: Cliopatria begins Castile in 961; the pages put the county's reunification and break with León in 931 (three pages agree), so the dossier starts in 931 with a new keyframe and the Leon dossier cuts the County of Castile out of its shapes from 931. Neither page gives a boundary or says when the rebellion became recognised independence (the Ramiro II page, read for the Leon dossier, has brief de facto independence only late in Ramiro's reign). (2) The county is also the Kingdom of Castile of Cliopatria: a rename in 1065 (kingdom proclaimed with Sancho II), one state, one colour. (3) Union years: Cliopatria draws the realm of one king as the Castile row 1046-1065, 1072-1125 and 1139-1168 and as the León row 1126-1138, and draws the two apart 1040-1045 and 1066-1071; this dossier keeps that allocation and records the passes as gain/loss events with kingdom-of-leon as counterpart (1046 conf 1, 1065, 1072, 1126, 1139 conf 1, 1157), mirroring the Leon dossier. The neighbour dossiers use kingdom-of-leon for events of 'León-Castile' in the same years (taifa-of-badajoz 1055 and 1064, almoravid-dynasty 1094, almohad-caliphate 1188-1202), while the land is drawn in the Castile row: the reviewer should reconcile the counterparts. (4) 1126-1138: Cliopatria draws no Castile; castile_1126 (the 1139 shape minus León 1126, 161 cells) fills it. (5) 1157: Cliopatria keeps the union as Castile to 1168; the division is August 1157 (castile_1157 and leon_1157). (6) 1195-1211: Cliopatria keeps Ciudad Real (Calatrava) in Castile through Alarcos and the Almohad reconquest; the Alfonso VIII page says the Almohads 'retook territory, starting with Calatrava' (the extent is the reading), restored in 1212 (conf 1). (7) 1216-1226: +39,400 km2 over 1202; only Baeza and Úbeda (1212) and Andújar/Baeza/Martos (1225) are dated by the pages; Albacete, southern Cuenca and Córdoba cells are unverified: page budget. (8) Portugal: the county-of-portugal dossier founds the county in 1096 (Henry of Burgundy); the Alfonso VI page says the date is disputed (not before 1103); Cliopatria drops the Portuguese lands from Castile in 1111. (9) End: the Castile row ends 1235 and the Crown of Castile row begins 1236 (Córdoba); the pages unite the crowns on 11 December 1230 (Ferdinand III page), 23 September 1230 (Kingdom of Castile infobox) or 10 December 1230 (Leon page). (10) Not read: Urraca's reign and the wars with Alfonso I of Aragon (1109-1126), Alfonso VII's 1135 homages, Ferdinand II of León's Extremadura, the Treaty of Cazola's content, Alfonso VIII's 1177-1179 Aragon wars, the military orders (Calatrava, Santiago) as landholders, Navarrese Gascony, Murcia and Seville. (11) Gazetteer names missing: Lamego, Baeza, Úbeda, Coria, Andújar, Martos, Briviesca, Sintra, Alarcos, Calatrava la Vieja: used as coordinates. (12) Rulers omitted: the Kingdom of Castile page's fetch kept only 'Sancho II (1065-1072)' and 'Ferdinand III (1217-1230)'. Page budget: nine pages; Ferdinand I, Alfonso VI and VII are shared with the Leon dossier.
